la:verb:cohorto.html:
cŏhorto, āre, 1, v. a. (rare collat. form of cohortor),
to exhort, encourage: et dicerent castra capta esse, atque hos cohortarent uti maturarent, Quadrig. ap. : exercitus pransus, paratus, cohortatus, Cat. ap. ; v. cohortor.

la:verb:cohortor.html:
cŏ-hortor, ātus, 1, v. dep.,
to animate or encourage by forcible language, to incite, exhort, admonish.
Esp., of the general before a battle, or in other milit. proceedings: cohortatus suos proelium commisit,: acies instruenda, milites cohortandi, signum dandum,: exercitum ad pugnam,: militem ad proelium,.—
With inf., Auct. B. Alex. 21; cf. .—
With ut or ne: Scipionis milites cohortatur, ut, etc.,; : ipse adit reliquos, cohortatur, ne labori succumbant,; cf. II.—
In gen., and without the sphere of military operations (in good prose).
Absol.: hac (eloquentiā) et cohortamur, hac persuademus,; : vereor ne majorem vim ad deterrendum habuerit quam ad cohortandum,.—
Aliquem: Caesar Remos cohortatus liberaliterque oratione prosecutus,; cf.: non sibi cohortandum Sulpicium, sed magis conlaudandum videri,.—
Aliquem ad aliquid: aliquem ad virtutem,: in hominibus ad virtutis studium cohortandis, : ad studium summae laudis,: ad pacem. , A, 3: ad concordiam,: ad libertatem recuperandam,. —
With final clause; with ut: fratrem cohortatus, ut, etc.,.—With ne: cohortantibus invicem, ne, etc.,.

la:verb:cohibeo.gloss: to hold together, contain, confine, comprise
senses: to hold together, contain, confine, comprise

la:verb:cohibeo.html:
cŏ-hĭbĕo, ui (
perf. subj. cohibessit, Lachm.), ĭtum, 2, v. a.
habeo
.
To hold together, to hold, contain, confine, embrace, comprise (class.; syn. contineo): omnes naturas ipsa (universa natura) cohibet et continet,; ; ; : (nubes) ut fumus constare nequirent, Nec cohibere nives gelidas et grandinis imbres,: aliquid in se,; cf. : at Scyllam caecis cohibet spelunca latebris,: semen occaecatum,: nodo crinem,: namque marem cohibent callosa (ova) vitellum,: auro lacertos,to encircle,: bracchium togā,: deos parietibus,.—
Trop. (very rare): sed interest inter causas fortuito antegressas, et inter causas cohibentis in se efficientiam naturalem, .—
With the access. idea of hindering free motion, to hold, keep, keep back, hinder, stay, restrain, stop, etc. (in a lit. sense in prose rare, but trop. very freq.).
Prop.: cohibete intra limen etiam vos parumper,: nec muris cohibet patriis media Ardea Turnum,: carcere ventos,: ventos in antris,: cervos arcu, to stop, poet. for to kill, : nec Stygiā cohibebor undā,: tempestatibus in portibus cohiberi, Auct. B. Afr. 98: cohiberi in vinculis,: Pirithoum cohibent catenae,: claustra cohibentia Janum,: ab aliquā re,; : sanguis spongiā in aceto tinctā cohibendus est,; cf. : alvum,: milites intra castra,: aquilones jugis montium,.—
Trop.
Cohibere aliquid or cohibere se, to stop something (or one's self), to hold in check, to restrain, limit, confine, keep back, repress, tame, subdue (syn.: contineo, refreno, arceo, coerceo): motus animi perturbatos,: furentis impetus crudelissimosque conatus,; cf.: furorem alicujus,: temeritatem,: gaudia clausa in sinu tacito,iras,: pravas aliorum spes,: ac premeret sensus suos,: bellum,: malum,: sumptus,: violentias effrenati doloris,: altitudinem aedificiorum,: (provinciae) quae procuratoribus cohibentur,i. e. are ruled,: non tu te cohibes? be moderate in grief, * ; so Sulp. ap. ; .—
With quominus: vix cohibuere amici, quominus eodem mari oppeteret,.—Pass.: ne flumine quidem interjecto, cohiberi quominus, etc.,.—
With inf., (but in ; ; Auct. B. G. 8, 23, prohibere is the true reading).—
Aliquid ab aliquā re or aliquo, to keep something from something (or somebody), to ward off: manus ab alieno,: manus, oculos, animum ab auro gazāque regiā,: effrenatas suas libidines a liberis et a conjugibus vestris,: adsensionem a rebus incertis,.—Hence, cŏhĭbĭtus, a, um, P. a., confined, limited, moderate: dicendi genus,.—Comp.: habitudo cohibitior,.

senses: a military unit of about 500 to 600 men
la:noun:cohors.html:
cŏhors (or cors; cf. ; later aspirated orthog. of MSS. chors; cf. the letter C, and Schne), rtis, f.
Sanscr. root har, rapio; cf.

Gr. χορός

.
A place enclosed around, a court, enclosure, yard, pen, etc., esp. for cattle, poultry, etc.
Cohors, ; ; Cato ap. Müll.; ; ; .—
Cors, Varr. ap. Non. l. l.; Glaucia ap. ; ; ; ; ; .—
Meton. (cf. chorus).
Lit., the multitude enclosed, fenced in; hence, in milit. lang., a company of soldiers, a division of an army, a cohort, the tenth part of a legion, comprising three manipuli or six centuriae (always written cohors), ; Cincius ap. ; ; so ; ; ; ; ; : praetoria, the prœtorian or bodyguard of the general, ; —Hence, trop.: habere scortorum cohortem praetoriam,.—
Opp. legiones, auxiliary troops, allies, ; ; ; .—
A troop of cavalry: centurio cohortis sextae equestris, (107) sq.—
Per synecdochen, an army in gen.: cohors Inachiae servatrix,.—
Specif., the train or retinue of the prœtor in a province: praetoria,; cf. , § 66; ; ; ; .—
In gen., a crowd, multitude, company, throng, attendants (mostly poet. or in post-Aug. prose): vaga,: gigantum,: fratrum stipata,; cf. ; ; : amicarum,of courtiers,; ; : canum,: oratorum,: sectatorum,.—Of things: febrium,.

la:verb:cohaereo.gloss: to cling, cleave or stick (closely) together; to be united, cohere, adhere
senses: to cling, cleave or stick (closely) together; to be united, cohere, adhere
to be composed of, consist of or in
to be near, close or united
to be closely connected, belong together
to be consistent (with), agree (together), to be in agreement (with), harmonize (with)
to hold oneself together, maintain oneself, remain, exist
to be in contact with or contiguous to
la:verb:cohaereo.html:
cŏ-haerĕo, haesi, haesum, 2, v. n.,
to cling together, to be united, either of that whose parts cling together, to cohere, or of that which cleaves to something else, to adhere.
Of a whole as composed of parts, or of the parts of a whole, to cling together, be united, to cohere, press or crowd together.
Lit.
In gen.: mundus ita apte cohaeret, ut dissolvi nullo modo queat, nisi ab eodem a quo est colligatus,: omnia autem duo ad cohaerendum tertium aliquid anquirunt et quasi nodum vinculumque desiderant,: neque enim materiam ipsam cohaerere potuisse, si nullā vi contineretur,: omni naturā cohaerente et continuatā,: nec res ulla magis primoribus ex elementis Indupedita suis arte conexa cohaeret Quam validi ferri natura,: solidā primordia... Quae minimis stipata cohaerent partibus arte,; : inter se juga velut serie cohaerentia,continuous,.—Of persons in a throng, etc.: alii extremo complexu suorum cohaerentes,; so of soldiers in line of battle: conferti et quasi cohaerentes tela vibrare non poterant,; and of two contending armies: duae quippe acies ita cohaerebant, ut armis arma pulsarent,; of ships: binas quadriremes Macedones inter se ita junxerant, ut prorae cohaererent,: conexis et cohaerentibus aedificiis, * .—
Pregn., to consist in or of, be composed of; with abl. (rare): cum alia quibus cohaererent homines e mortali genere sumpserint, quae fragilia essent et caduca, animum esse ingeneratum a deo,; cf.: mundus omnibus partibus inter se congruentibus cohaeret et nititur, etc., ap. .—
Trop.
Of persons united by kindred, friendship, etc., to be near, close, united: turpes ac perniciosos, etiamsi nobis sanguine cohaereant, amputandos,: est enim mihi perjucundum quod viri optimi mihique amicissimi adeo cohaesistis ut invicem vos obligari putetis,.—
Of things.
In discourse, to belong together, be closely connected: quae... si suis quaeque temporibus reddere voluero, interrumpendae sunt res Asiae, quas... sicut inter se cohaerent, ita opere ipso conjungi aptius videri potest,.—
In thought, to be consistent, agree together: em, Paululum obsoni, ipsus tristis, de inproviso nuptiae—Non cohaerent,i.e. cannot all be here at once,: tam eras excors, ut... non modo non cohaerentia inter se diceres, sed maxime dijuncta atque contraria,: dubitandum non est quin numquam possit utilitas cum honestate contendere. Itaque accepimus Socratem exsecrari solitum eos qui primum haec naturā cohaerentia opinione distraxissent,: non quaero jam, verumne sit: illud dico, ea, quae dicat, praeclare inter se cohaerere,: animadvertisti, quam multa dicta sint, quamque, etiam si minus vera, tamen apta inter se et cohaerentia,: male cohaerens cogitatio,: sensus inter se juncti, atque ita cohaerentes, ne, etc.,; ; : sermo hercule familiaris et cottidianus non cohaerebit, si verba inter nos aucupamur,have a consistent meaning, be intelligible,: vix diserti adulescentis cohaerebat oratio,; and of harmony in the arrangement of words: conlocabuntur igitur verba, ut aut inter se aptissime cohaereant extrema cum primis eaque sint quam suavissimis vocibus, etc., : haec collocatio verborum ... quae junctam orationem efficit, quae cohaerentem, etc.,; .—
Pregn., to hold together, i.e. remain, exist, maintain itself: omnibus modis fulciendi sunt, qui ruunt nec cohaerere possunt propter magnitudinem aegritudinis,: virtutes sine vitā beatā cohaerere non possunt, nec sine virtute vita beata,: vix haec, si undique fulciamus, jam labefacta... nixa in omnium nostrum umeris cohaerebunt,.—
To cling closely to something else, to adhere, be connected with, cleave to, be in contact with, etc.
Lit.
With dat.: temptanti dextera flxa est Cuspide Marmaridae Corythi, lignoque cohaesit,; : nec equo mea membra cohaerent,: scopuloque affixa cohaesit,: fructus quamdiu solo cohaerent,: superficies... quae natura solo cohaeret,: quippe turris... muris hostium propemodum cohaerebat,: experimentum marmorati est in subigendo donec rutro non cohaereat,: qui cohaerent Mesopotamiae Rhoali vocantur,adjoin,.—
With cum and abl.: quidquid enim sequitur quamque rem, id cohaeret cum re necessario,.—
With in and abl.: cohaerentis videmus in conchis (margaritas), etc.,.—
Absol.: jamque ea (navis) quae non cohaerebat,i.e. which did not collide,.—
Trop., to be closely connected with, in agreement or harmony with something else, to be consistent with: quod illa, quae prima dicuntur, si vehementer velis congruere et cohaerere cum causā, ex eis ducas oportet, quae post dicenda sunt,: si continget, etiam (id quod fingemus) verae alicui rei cohaereat,: ut non tamquam citharoedi prooemium adfictum aliquid, sed cohaerens cum omni corpore membrum videatur,: creditis tot gentes... non sacris, non moribus, non commercio linguae nobiscum cohaerentes, eodem proelio domitas esse, etc.,: potentia male cohaerens inter Pompeium et Caesarem,.—
To be vitally connected with, to depend upon a thing; with abl.: sed ita legibus Sullae cohaerere statum civitatis adfirmat, ut iis solutis stare ipsa non possit,.—Hence,
cŏhae-rens, entis, P. a. (cohering, i.e.), being in accord, corresponding: aptius et cohaerentius,.—*
cŏhaerenter, adv., continuously, uninterruptedly: dimicatum est,.—
cŏhaesus, a, um. P. a., pressed together: quercus stricta denuo et cohaesa,.
